title: A2A in Agent Framework and Foundry
summary: Microsoft Agent Framework and Foundry Agent Service can both call and expose A2A agents. Foundry's a2a tool and A2A 1.0 are generally available, while the Agent Framework A2A packages are prerelease, and each has limits worth knowing.
useIf: You build on Microsoft's stack and need agents to call, or be called by, agents on other platforms.
avoidIf: Your agents share one process and team: Agent Framework's agent-as-tool pattern is simpler and cheaper.

explain.md: **Calling** a remote agent: Agent Framework's `A2AAgent` wraps any A2A endpoint as a normal agent, so `run` and streaming work as usual. You can resolve a card from a well-known URI (`A2ACardResolver`), start from a card you got from a registry, or configure the endpoint directly. The .NET client prefers HTTP+JSON over JSON-RPC unless you set `PreferredBindings`. A long task returns a continuation token you can poll or resubscribe to, and the A2A `context_id`, `task_id` and `task_state` live in the session [[r15]]. `A2AAgent` is only a transport wrapper: the remote agent's tools stay invisible and are changed on the remote side [[r15]].

**Exposing** an agent: .NET uses `Microsoft.Agents.AI.Hosting.A2A.AspNetCore` (`AddA2AServer`, `MapA2AHttpJson`, `MapWellKnownAgentCard`). Python uses `A2AExecutor` from `agent-framework-a2a`, built on `a2a-sdk`, which maps agent output to A2A events and artifacts and passes the A2A `context_id` as the session id. Go uses `a2aprovider`. You author and publish the Agent Card yourself. Install the packages with `--prerelease` (.NET) or `--pre` (Python): they are prerelease as of 2026-10-13 [[r14]].

pitfalls.symptom: Replies arrive in the 0.3 shape from a Foundry agent
pitfalls.cause: No `A2A-Version` header or `a2a-version` query value was sent, so Foundry served 0.3
pitfalls.fix: Send `A2A-Version: 1.0`, or let the client fetch the v1.0 card so the SDK negotiates [[r17]]

pitfalls.symptom: Package install fails or resolves an old version
pitfalls.cause: The A2A packages are prerelease and need `--prerelease` (.NET) or `--pre` (Python)
pitfalls.fix: Pass the flag and pin the version in your lock file [[r14]]

pitfalls.symptom: Conversation context vanishes after a restart
pitfalls.cause: The session with `context_id`, `task_id` and `task_state` was not persisted, or the remote agent expired it
pitfalls.fix: Persist the session (`to_dict`) and design for retention limits (Foundry keeps 60 days from last write) [[r15]] [[r17]]

scenarios.title: A .NET orchestrator calling a partner and a Foundry agent
scenarios.situation: A .NET orchestrator must call a partner's Python agent and a team's Foundry prompt agent. Both publish A2A cards. The partner's job may run for 20 minutes.
unknowns: Which A2A versions do the peers serve?
How do the peers authenticate callers?
scenarios.question: How does the orchestrator call them?

options.name: `A2AAgent` per peer, resolved from cards, with background responses for the long job
options.why: One programming model for both peers, continuation tokens for the 20-minute task and card-driven interface choice.
options.tradeoff: Prerelease packages and your own auth handling per peer.

options.name: REST function tools written per peer
options.why: Full control and no prerelease dependency.
options.tradeoff: You rebuild tasks, context ids and polling for the long job.

options.name: The Connected Agents tool
options.why: It is not available in the new Foundry Agent Service.
options.tradeoff: Right only for legacy classic agents that still run.

flips.if: The orchestrator is itself a Foundry agent
flips.then: Use the `a2a` tool with a project connection.
Use plain REST tools and accept the extra code.

scenarios.takeaway: Use the SDK that models tasks and context ids for you.

scenarios.title: Exposing an agent that streams and returns files
scenarios.situation: Another team wants live progress and a generated PDF from your agent over A2A. Your agent currently runs as a Foundry prompt agent.
constraints: Callers need streaming and file artifacts
Foundry incoming A2A is text-only and non-streaming
unknowns: Can callers accept polling and a link in text?
scenarios.question: How do you expose it?

options.name: Self-host an Agent Framework A2A server with streaming and artifacts
options.why: You control bindings, streaming and artifact parts, which Foundry's incoming endpoint does not offer for v1.0.
options.tradeoff: You run hosting, auth and scaling, and depend on prerelease packages.

options.name: Foundry incoming A2A with polling and a download link in text
options.why: Managed endpoint with Entra auth and no hosting work.
options.tradeoff: No live progress and files only by reference.

options.name: Foundry incoming A2A with files base64-encoded into text
options.why: Large payloads in text break limits and clients cannot treat them as files.

flips.if: Callers only need a text answer
Foundry later declares streaming for v1.0 on its card
flips.then: Re-evaluate and move back to the managed endpoint.

scenarios.takeaway: Match the host to the modalities and streaming you must support.

quiz.q: Which Foundry A2A tool type targets A2A 1.0 and is generally available?
quiz.explain: `a2a` targets 1.0 and is GA, `a2a_preview` targets 0.3 and is Preview, and Connected Agents is not in the new Foundry Agent Service. `mcp` is a different protocol.

quiz.q: Match each item to its platform behaviour.

pairs.r: JSON-RPC only, text only, no streaming

quiz.explain: These are the four platform facts checked on 2026-10-13: Foundry's v1.0 limits, the transport-only wrapper, the 0.3 default and the prerelease status.

quiz.q: A team calls a Foundry agent over A2A without any version selector and the reply shapes look like the old protocol. What explains it?
options: The agent was deployed with the wrong model
Foundry serves A2A 0.3 when no version is selected
quiz.explain: Without an `A2A-Version` header or `a2a-version` query value Foundry serves preview 0.3. The model, binding and card signature do not decide the protocol version.

flashcards.front: Which Foundry A2A tool type is GA and for which protocol version?
flashcards.back: `a2a` for A2A 1.0 (GA). `a2a_preview` is for 0.3 and is Preview.

flashcards.front: What are the limits of Foundry's incoming A2A for v1.0?
flashcards.back: JSON-RPC only, text modality only, no streaming, Entra auth only, tasks and contexts kept 60 days from last write.

flashcards.front: How do you install the Agent Framework A2A packages?
flashcards.back: `--prerelease` for .NET packages and `--pre` for `agent-framework-a2a` in Python. They are prerelease as of 2026-10-13.
